evidence.quote: The city comptroller's office has opened a formal investigation into travel reimbursement requests filed by Samantha Reeves, deputy director of the parks and recreation department, after an internal audit flagged a pattern of expense claims that could not be matched to corresponding travel records.

Reeves has been placed on paid administrative leave while the investigation proceeds, a standard step the city said it takes whenever a department official is the subject of an active financial review.
Reeves remains on paid administrative leave and has not been charged with any offense.
'Ms. Reeves has cooperated fully with every request from the comptroller's office, and we expect this to be resolved once they've had a chance to review what we've submitted,' Webb said.

The parks and recreation department named deputy director Samantha Reeves its 2025 Employee of the Year at last December's staff recognition dinner, citing her work expanding the department's after-school sports programming to five additional neighborhoods.
Reeves, who has worked for the department for nine years, was credited with securing a state grant that funded new equipment for three community centers.
Department director Thomas Lee said at the time that Reeves' organizational skills and attention to detail had made her one of the most reliable members of his leadership team.
